To answer this request we have assembled the following team:

- review-provenance-producer: <no description, use name to identify the purpose of this participant>
- review-provenance-verifier: <no description, use name to identify the purpose of this participant>


Here is an initial fact sheet to consider:

## 1. GIVEN OR VERIFIED FACTS

- The approved scope is limited to the review-provenance core.
- Required capabilities are:
  - A review-only, immutable orchestration amendment mechanism.
  - Early canonical Shaper-intent validation.
  - Early chartered Delivery Lead plan validation.
  - Protocol-v8 envelope-limit validation.
  - Focused tests.
  - Generated process documentation.
- Original authority and compatibility must be preserved.
- Explicitly excluded:
  - Claude provider-adapter repairs.
  - Codex provider-adapter repairs.
  - Editing run artifacts.
  - Applying the amendment to `maf-runtime-readiness-2`.
- The isolated worktree is pinned to commit `5ac43343b83e2b1c9168508ebd3609ad40251771`.
- The approved baseline is clean.
- Read-only analyst and verifier specialists may analyze only the supplied task text; they cannot inspect files, execute commands, or edit the worktree.
- The approved editor may modify only paths permitted by the charter.
- Flow verifies the resulting diff and runs the targeted test after the edit.
- The full test suite is an acceptance check.
- Approved editors receive exactly one call in total.
- Flow refuses a second editor call.
- The editor’s single call must both inspect the necessary repository content and complete all edits.
- An inspect-only editor call, or an instruction not to edit yet, would fail the attempt because Flow checks the worktree immediately afterward.
- Work must remain within the provided workspace.
- Subagents and delegation are prohibited.

## 2. FACTS TO LOOK UP

- The charter’s exact allowed file paths, in the repository’s Flow charter or equivalent execution metadata.
- Existing review and orchestration data models, APIs, and persistence rules, in the source tree pinned to the stated commit.
- The canonical representation and validation rules for Shaper intent, in existing schemas, validators, protocol definitions, and tests.
- The definition of a chartered Delivery Lead plan and its required validation constraints, in charter, planning, workflow, and validation code.
- Protocol-v8 envelope fields and precise size or count limits, in protocol-v8 schemas, constants, documentation, and compatibility tests.
- Existing authority boundaries that must remain unchanged, in orchestration policies, role definitions, authorization checks, and relevant tests.
- Existing backward-compatibility expectations, in public interfaces, fixtures, migration logic, changelogs, and regression tests.
- The project’s expected amendment immutability semantics, in review models, audit/provenance code, and process documentation.
- The focused targeted-test command Flow expects, in repository configuration, charter metadata, or contributor documentation.
- The generator and source templates used for process documentation, in documentation tooling and generated-file headers.
- The locations of run artifacts and `maf-runtime-readiness-2`, so they can be confirmed as out of scope and left untouched.
- Any repository-specific instructions such as `AGENTS.md`, contribution rules, formatting configuration, and test conventions.

## 3. FACTS TO DERIVE

- Which concrete files fall within both the requested scope and the charter’s edit allowlist.
- The smallest implementation that satisfies all four approved capabilities without changing existing authority.
- Where validation must occur to qualify as “early” while preserving compatibility.
- How to distinguish review-only amendments from executable or authority-changing orchestration updates.
- How to guarantee amendment immutability, including whether append-only storage, frozen values, defensive copies, or mutation rejection is required.
- How amendments reference the original orchestration state without replacing or silently modifying it.
- Which Shaper-intent form is canonical and how noncanonical or malformed intent must fail.
- How to determine whether a Delivery Lead plan is chartered and which invalid plans must be rejected before execution.
- Exact protocol-v8 boundary cases, including values immediately below, at, and above each envelope limit.
- Which legacy inputs must continue to succeed unchanged.
- The focused test cases needed to prove successful amendment creation, mutation prevention, early validation failures, envelope-limit boundaries, exclusions, and compatibility.
- Whether generated documentation is reproducible and synchronized with its authoritative source.
- Whether the final diff touches only permitted paths and avoids all explicitly excluded work.
- Whether targeted and full-suite results satisfy acceptance without relying on provider-adapter repairs.

## 4. EDUCATED GUESSES

- “Review-only” likely means an amendment records reviewer-proposed orchestration changes without granting execution authority or mutating the accepted orchestration.
- “Immutable” likely requires creating a new amendment record rather than updating an existing amendment or the original orchestration.
- “Preserve original authority” likely means reviewer amendments cannot impersonate, supersede, or acquire the Shaper’s or Delivery Lead’s authority.
- Canonical Shaper-intent validation likely belongs at the earliest orchestration ingestion or construction boundary.
- Chartered Delivery Lead plan validation likely belongs before scheduling, dispatch, persistence, or provider invocation.
- Protocol-v8 envelope validation likely requires deterministic rejection at documented maximum boundaries before downstream processing.
- Compatibility likely requires existing valid payloads and public call patterns to retain their current behavior.
- Focused tests will likely emphasize rejection timing, immutable provenance, authority separation, boundary values, and regression coverage.
- Generated process documentation likely must be produced from repository-owned templates or schemas rather than edited only as standalone prose.
- The prohibited provider-adapter repairs are probably known adjacent failures that must not be folded into this narrowly approved change.


Here is the plan to follow as best as possible:

- Have `review-provenance-verifier` analyze the supplied requirements and identify scope boundaries, acceptance criteria, compatibility risks, and required validation cases without accessing the repository.
- Give `review-provenance-producer` the single authorized editor call, explicitly requiring it to inspect the repository and complete the entire implementation in that same call, only within charter-approved paths.
- In that call, implement the immutable review-only amendment mechanism, early Shaper-intent and Delivery Lead plan validation, protocol-v8 envelope limits, focused tests, and generated process documentation.
- Preserve existing authority and compatible behavior; exclude provider-adapter repairs, run artifacts, and any amendment to `maf-runtime-readiness-2`.
- Let Flow verify the allowed-path diff and run the targeted test immediately after the edit, then run the full suite as the acceptance check.
- Report the resulting changes, targeted-test result, full-suite result, and confirmation that all prohibited areas remained untouched.
